items.title: Karnataka HC rejects plea against S Vidyashankar's appointment as VC of Visvesvaraya University
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has dismissed an appeal challenging the appointment of Dr S Vidyashankar as Vice-Chancellor of Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) at Belagavi [Yogesh B v. State of Karnataka]. A bench of Justice D K Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan said that Court's constitutional jurisdiction cannot be invoked repeatedly to unsettle an appointment in the absence of a clear legal infirmity. "The dignity of the office and the sanctity of the judicial process demand that both the office-holder and those who invoke the jurisdiction of the Court act with restraint, bona fides and fidelity to law," it added. Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan The Court said the petitioner had not been able to demonstrate that Vidyashankar suffers from any statutory disqualification which could render him ineligible to hold the office of Vice-Chancellor. "There is equally no material of such a nature as would establish that the appointment was made by an authority lacking jurisdiction or in patent violation of a mandatory statutory requirement," it added. The appeal arose from a petition filed by Yogesh B and Venugopal KA, who had questioned Vidyashankar's continuance as VTU Vice-Chancellor through a writ of quo warranto. The petitioners had challenged the original appointment notification dated September 29, 2022, alleging violations of the UGC Regulations, 2018 and Section 13 of the VTU Act, 1994. They had also questioned the constitution of the Search-cum-Selection Committee, including the alleged absence of a UGC nominee, and raised objections concerning Vidyashankar's academic credentials and antecedents. After the petitioners failed to secure any relief from a single judge, Yogesh B filed an appeal in the matter. On September 10, the Court ruled that the appellant had failed to establish any statutory disqualification or patent illegality in Vidyashankar's appointment warranting issuance of a writ of quo warranto. "It is not enough for a petitioner merely to assert that the selection was irregular or that another person was more meritorious. What is required to be established is that the incumbent is holding the office without lawful authority. That essential requirement has not been satisfied in the present case," the Bench said. items.title: Advocate not above the law: J&K High Court on lawyer's plea against police request for assistance
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh recently observed that merely being an advocate does not place a person above the law and that, as an officer of the court, a lawyer is expected to render lawful assistance to an investigating agency when required [Wasim Ahmed Reshi V/s UT of JK and others]. At the same time, the High Court cautioned the police that they are equally bound to act strictly in accordance with law and directed the investigating agency to scrupulously follow the prescribed procedure whenever it seeks the presence or assistance of an advocate during an investigation. “Merely because the petitioner is an advocate does not place him above the law. Rather, being an officer of the court and well versed with the legal position, he is expected to render such lawful assistance to the investigating agency as may be required so that the truth concerning the alleged offence is brought to light and, if an offence has indeed been committed, the offender is brought to justice. Such cooperation is in consonance with the administration of justice and the duties expected of an officer of the Court,” the High Court said. items.title: The new Labour Codes and their impact on Global Capability Centres
items.summary: As is widely known, 29 separate central labour statutes, each with its own definitions, thresholds and procedures have now been repealed and consolidated into 4 Codes: the Code on Wages, 2019; the Industrial Relations Code, 2020; the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020; and the Code on Social Security, 2020 (together, the “Codes”), which came into force on November 21, 2025. Central rules under all four Codes were subsequently notified on 8 and 9 May 2026, operationalising the Codes at the central level. However, several states, including some with large global capability centre (“GCC”) clusters, are yet to notify their own state-specific rules, and therefore several of the erstwhile positions continue to apply. This article sets out (I) how the new regime differs from the old one and its impact on the GCCs, and (II) how compliance risk needs to be factored in across the different models of GCCs. Comparison between the old and the new regime and its impact on GCCs Restructuring of wages Under the old regime, “wages” was defined separately and inconsistently across several statutes. Under the new regime, wages are defined only under the Code on Wages, 2019, as basic pay, dearness allowance and retaining allowance, plus other components (including house rent allowance and conveyance allowance) where and to the extent these exceed 50% of total remuneration. For GCCs, this means compensation structures where basic pay has been kept low relative to allowances will need to be reviewed. Provident fund and gratuity liabilities will rise wherever the 50% threshold brings allowances into wages, increasing statutory provident fund and gratuity contributions. Total cost-to-company will typically rise as a result, unless fixed and variable pay components are restructured to offset the change. Full and final settlement Previously, the two working day payment deadline applied only where the exit was employer-initiated (discharge, dismissal, retrenchment) or the establishment closed; no equivalent statutory deadline applied to a resignation. Under the new regime, all wages must be paid within two working days of the last working day regardless of whether the exit is a resignation, termination or retrenchment. This deadline applies to wages as newly defined and gratuity, provident fund and other dues continue to follow their own separate statutory timelines. items.title: Delhi High Court bars misuse of AI deepfakes infringing Rajat Sharma’s personality rights
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has permanently barred various online video channels, individuals and online entities (defendants) from circulating deepfake videos and images of journalist Rajat Sharma and India TV and misusing Sharma’s personality attributes [Rajat Sharma Vs Tamara Doc]. Justice Jyoti Singh restrained the defendants from infringing Sharma’s personality and publicity rights as well as India TV’s intellectual property rights. The order was passed on August 24. Justice Jyoti Singh Sharma and India TV had approached the Court seeking protection against infringement of his personality and publicity rights, infringement of India TV’s registered trademarks, misappropriation of goodwill, unfair trade practices and copyright violations. They alleged that several defendants were spreading misinformation through artificial intelligence-generated doctored videos containing distorted and modified images, voices and other personality traits of Sharma. They also alleged unauthorised use of India TV’s registered trademarks and violation of its copyright. In December 2024, the High Court had passed an ex parte interim order restraining several defendants from infringing Sharma’s personality and publicity rights and India TV’s intellectual property. Meta was then directed to block or remove the impugned content and disclose details of the concerned defendants. The Department of Telecommunications and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology were also directed to facilitate the blocking of infringing websites, telephone numbers, social-media accounts and channels. During the pendency of the suit, four YouTube channels were made party to the case after they were accused of circulating deepfake videos using Sharma’s personality attributes. In November 2025, Google was directed to take down some of these YouTube channels and disclose available subscriber information, IP logs and other account details. The defendants, against whom the suit was eventually decreed, had been served but failed to file written statements. Their right to do so was closed by the Joint Registrar in July 2026. The Court also gave Sharma and India TV liberty to directly approach Meta and Google with details of any fresh URLs or content involving misuse of Sharma’s name, likeness, image, voice, photographs or videos. items.title: Law, music and cinema not strangers to each other: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana at NUALS seminar
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana on Friday drew parallels between law, music and cinema observing that all three involve interpretation and making sense of human experiences within their respective frameworks. Drawing a parallel between music and law, the judge said that while music has rules, rhythm structure and harmony which help an artist create music, so does law which has Constitution, legislation and procedure which provides a framework within which judges and lawyers work. " Law is not entirely different, the Constitution, legislation and procedure give us our framework, they tell us where the boundaries are and so judges are constantly trying to do something quite delicate; to interpret law faithfully while recognising that the world in which the law operates is constantly changing. The answer to why art matters to law is rather simple. We spend a great deal of time in law dealing with categories, principles and procedures. But behind every case is a person, behind every legal dispute is a human experience, " Justice Mohana said. She was speaking at the inaugural ceremony of the ' Three-day Seminar on Music, Cinema and Law: Exploring the Intersections of Art, Culture and Law ,' jointly organised by the Kerala Judicial Academy and the National University of Advanced Studies (NUALs) at Bolgatty in Kochi. The seminar was inaugurated by Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan in the presence of Justice Mohana, Kerala High Court Chief Justice Soumen Sen , Justice Anil K Narendran , Minister of Higher Education Roji M John, other judges, lawyers, academics and members of the creative community. items.title: Regulating arbitrators like Supreme Court, High Court judges is impossible: Retired Justice AK Sikri
items.summary: It would be impossible to regulate arbitrators in exactly the same manner as Supreme Court and High Court judges, former Supreme Court Justice AK Sikri said during a debate at India ADR Week 2026. Justice Sikri was one of the judges for the Oxford-style debate on whether arbitrators should be professionally regulated like judges. Judging the debate along him were Dentons Link Legal Managing Partner Atul Sharma and Carsten van de Sande of Hengeler Mueller. The debate was moderated by Saraf & Partners partner Sanya Sud . Justice Sikri said that the proposition itself could be understood in two ways: either that arbitrators should be subject to some form of regulation similar to judges, or that they should be regulated through the same mechanisms applicable to judges. If the latter interpretation were adopted, the proposition would fail, he said. “As I understood the parties and both the sides kept in mind the higher judicial service only, that is High Court and Supreme Court judges. And how these judges are regulated, I think, it is impossible to have that kind of regulation for the arbitrators. ” Arguing for the motion, Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas Partner Binsy Susan said that arbitrators exercise substantial adjudicatory power without an equivalent professional disciplinary framework. Along with M&Co Legal Partner Tariq Khan, she argued that the proposal was about functional parity in professional standards, not identical tenure, salaries or constitutional status. Susan pointed out that lawyers are answerable to professional bodies, while a person acting as an arbitrator may not face an equivalent complaints mechanism. items.title: Chennai: 285 with criminal records detained in crime prevention drive
items.summary: Nearly 285 people with criminal records, including history-sheeters, were arrested in a special drive conducted across Chennai, with police claiming that the operation was aimed at preventing crime and curbing the activities of habitual offenders. They were detained during an intensive search operation carried out from Thursday, September 10 night to Friday, September 11 evening, following directions from Greater Chennai Police Commissioner A Amalraj. The operation was conducted under the supervision of Deputy Commissioners and led by Assistant Commissioners, Inspectors and other police personnel. Of the 285 people detained, 108 were from the North Zone, 38 from the West Zone, 94 from the South Zone and 45 from the East Zone. “During the operation, the teams detained 285 individuals with criminal backgrounds, whose history sheets are maintained at various police stations in the city. They are being questioned to ascertain their current activities and possible involvement in recent offences,” a senior police officer said. However, the police's classification of people as having “criminal backgrounds” or being history-sheeters does not, by itself, establish that they have committed a recent offence. History sheets are police records maintained on people considered to have criminal antecedents, and the use of such records for preventive policing has previously raised concerns over surveillance, arbitrary detention and the targeting of people without a specific allegation against them. Police Commissioner Amalraj said such special drives would continue and that stringent legal action would be taken against those involved in criminal activities. He also instructed Additional Commissioners and other senior officers to closely monitor the movements of people with criminal antecedents, dangerous offenders and those released from prison on bail. Amalraj further directed officers to strengthen patrolling and vehicle checks and take stringent action against drunk driving.

items.title: At BRICS PM Modi reiterates call for ‘dialogue and diplomacy’ in talks with Putin
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, September 11, once again told Russian President Vladimir Putin that “dialogue and diplomacy” were the way forward to resolve the conflict in Ukraine. The Prime Minister met his Russian counterpart on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, PM Modi said India remained willing to contribute to peace efforts. The two leaders also discussed the Ukraine war and the conflict in West Asia, including their impact on maritime trade. The conversation came shortly after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar’s visit to Kyiv, where he said the Ukraine conflict could only be resolved through dialogue, diplomacy and negotiations. India has maintained its engagement with Russia, including its purchases of Russian oil, despite growing pressure from the West. The safety of shipping in the Black Sea also figured in the Modi-Putin talks. India had raised concerns with both Moscow and Kyiv after attacks on merchant vessels in July killed Indian seafarers. The meeting also covered the wider India-Russia partnership, with discussions spanning defence, energy, trade, industry, space and political cooperation. After the talks, Modi and Putin travelled together in the Russian president’s armoured Aurus Senat to the INNOPROM India exhibition at Bharat Mandapam. Their shared rides have become a familiar feature of recent meetings, including during Putin’s India visit in December 2025 and their meeting in Bishkek last month. At the BRICS Business Forum, Putin presented the grouping as an increasingly important force in the global economy, saying its members account for more than 40% of global GDP. He criticised Western sanctions and restrictions on trade, transport and energy infrastructure. His remarks come as India faces potential US penalties under legislation targeting major buyers of Russian oil and gas, adding another layer of pressure to New Delhi’s ties with Moscow. items.title: 17 days after Nepal floods, 85 TN pilgrims remain missing
items.summary: Of the 305 tourists from Tamil Nadu who got caught in the Nepal flash floods amid a pilgrimage, 220 have been rescued, while 85 remain missing. Seventeen days after the disaster, which occurred on August 26, families of 49 people who travelled to Nepal through a pilgrimage agency in Chromepet say they have received no updates from the Tamil Nadu government beyond being told that their relatives are yet to be traced. According to reports, DNA profiles of the relatives of 78 of the 85 missing Tamils have been handed over to the Nepal government. The Tamil Nadu government had announced on September 3 that free DNA tests would be conducted for first-degree relatives of pilgrims from the state who went missing in the Nepal flash floods. The tests are being conducted at forensic science laboratories in Chennai, Madurai and Thanjavur. The government had also instructed district collectors to make arrangements to take willing first-degree relatives to the nearest regional laboratory for blood sample collection. Their details would then be uploaded to the Nepal government's website to facilitate identification. The state government has also said it would provide assistance to relatives who wish to travel to Nepal, along with the required documents and details. The floods have emerged as one of Nepal's deadliest disasters in decades, with more than 1,300 people killed and thousands still missing. The floods, triggered by a massive glacial collapse on August 26, swept through several districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower facilities and leaving hundreds of workers trapped in tunnels. Rescue teams continue to recover bodies and, in some cases, find survivors days after the disaster. According to the Nepal government, reconstruction of the damaged infrastructure is expected to cost $4.78 billion. The Nepal government also intends to raise the issue at the United Nations to draw the attention of the international community to the repeated loss of life and property Nepal has faced due to climate change and climate-related disasters.

items.title: Union presses Keralam to take decision on PM SHRI scheme; UDF remains divided
items.summary: The Union government has asked the Keralam government to take a decision on implementing the PM SHRI scheme at the earliest. The direction has put pressure on the ruling UDF, which remains divided over the proposal. General Education Minister N Samsudheen said on Friday, September 11, that the Union Education Secretary had written to Keralam Chief Secretary seeking a decision on the scheme. The letter was received around two days ago. “The letter states that a decision must be taken at the earliest so that the remaining schemes can move forward. It has been two or three days since it was received. We will discuss it in this context,” Samsudheen told reporters. Samsudheen, who belongs to the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), said the UDF had differing views on the scheme and that its reservations remained. He said the final decision would be taken after discussions with Chief Minister V D Satheesan and other UDF leaders. “I cannot make a statement on my own. The Chief Minister, along with our UDF leadership, will decide, and the CM will make the announcement,” he said. “There are different perspectives. The UDF is against the scheme. We said it before the election. Even now we have opposing views,” Samsudheen said. The Union government’s communication is the second such letter received by the state, even as a Cabinet subcommittee appointed to examine the scheme is yet to meet. The government has sought a report from the four-member panel comprising Samsudheen, P C Vishnunadh, M Liju and Roji M John. The previous LDF government had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Union government to implement PM SHRI. However, criticism within the LDF, particularly from the CPI, and protests by the UDF led to the agreement being kept in abeyance. After the UDF came to power, the government had indicated that it would proceed with the scheme, citing the agreement signed by the previous government and funds that had been withheld by the Union government. The move, however, faced opposition from within the UDF, particularly the IUML, which has raised concerns that the scheme could facilitate the Sangh Parivar agenda in education. The government subsequently constituted the Cabinet subcommittee to examine the issue and recommend whether Keralam should proceed with the scheme or withdraw from it.
